scope: Audit Strata's existing one- and two-GPU Qwen optimization surfaces, B550's live topology, and the local K-Transformers checkout; define the matched benchmark required once a runnable Qwen GGUF pack exists. No model was downloaded, converted, loaded, run, or benchmarked in this task.

checkpoint_state_at_plan_time.boundary: The Qwen source safetensors checkpoint is not itself a runnable Strata artifact. Strata needs a supported GSQ-RCO or Unsloth GGUF set, prepared pack inputs, and the PLE table. A finished source transfer therefore gates conversion or a separately produced runnable artifact, not immediate model execution.

b550_topology.cpu: AMD Ryzen 9 5900XT, 16 cores / 32 threads, AVX2, no AVX-512
b550_topology.interconnect: nvidia-smi reports PHB between the cards; no NVLink
b550_topology.implication: A K-Transformers-style tensor-parallel allreduce would cross PCIe through the host. Strata's layer pipeline, helper expert caches, and CPU/GPU MoE placement are better matched to this topology. Both long-running embedding replicas must remain untouched; all arms will start with the same roughly 20.5 GiB free per card unless a later dedicated-run decision explicitly stops them.

code_verified: src/program/generate.cpp implements --layer-split, --split-device, --peer-device, --expert-cache-device1..3, --remote-expert-opt, --adapt-async, --pipeline-windows, --batch-groups, and PCIe share controls
serve/server.py treats several GPUs as a layer split unless --peer-device selects the alternate peer-expert tier
tools/calibrate.py already sweeps PCIe share, speculative draft threshold, CPU workers, and adaptive expert settings
bench/bench_vs_llama.py and tools/ab_engine.py provide paired server benchmark surfaces

modes.name: single GPU
modes.controls: one card, calibrated expert cache, adaptive tier, PCIe share, and speculative decoding
modes.purpose: the mandatory control; test each card because their maximum PCIe generations differ

modes.name: layer split
modes.controls: --gpus 0,1 or 1,0; --layer-split auto followed by a bounded manual K sweep; --trim-stage-weights
modes.purpose: pipeline model parallelism across layers and approximately double aggregate expert-cache capacity

modes.name: helper expert GPU
modes.purpose: keep one primary and assign a complementary hot-expert cache to the second card over pinned host buffers, avoiding a P2P requirement

modes.name: pipeline windows
modes.controls: --pipeline-windows 2, with --adapt-async 1 and STRATA_ADAPT_LAG/STRATA_EXCHANGE_ROTATE as follow-on arms
modes.purpose: overlap the next verify window across the two stages, primarily targeting prefill and pipeline stalls

modes.name: short-prompt peer help
modes.controls: STRATA_PREFILL_HELP=1 and STRATA_PREFILL_HELP_FRAC, separate from fused prefill
modes.purpose: let the otherwise idle stage stream some one-chunk prompt experts over its own PCIe link

modes.name: batched conversations
modes.purpose: measure aggregate multi-client throughput, not single-stream latency

strata_native_capability.not_appropriate_here: --peer-device is a separate P2P-oriented peer-expert tier and is incompatible with layer split/helper caches. B550 has no NVLink and reports PHB, so helper-cache and layer-split arms are the primary modes; a peer-device arm is optional only after cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer is proven live.

ktransformers_audit.local_delta: One commit changes kt-kernel/python/cli/utils/model_registry.py only, adding Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash registry entries. No K-Transformers code is imported by Strata.
portable_ideas: Hotness-aware GPU-resident experts: Strata already has the stronger native analogue in its expert profile, per-card expert caches, adaptive swaps, and helper complementary ownership.
CPU/GPU MoE split: Strata already owns a C++/CUDA CPU expert pool, pinned arena, PCIe share, and asynchronous adaptive exchanges.

Multi-GPU execution: K-Transformers leans on serving-framework tensor parallelism, while Strata has native layer split, helper expert caches, pipeline windows, and batch groups. These are different mechanisms; K-Transformers TP is not automatically superior on consumer PCIe.
The only immediately useful K-Transformers registry numbers as candidate workload bounds are chunked prefill 32768 and max total tokens 100000, not direct engine settings.
do_not_port: The archived module-replacement YAML machinery and KT-Kernel method registry do not map onto Strata's compiled engine.
Deferred CPU experts from the older research path; prior work identified output-corrupting behavior.
AMX, dual-NUMA, and SM120-only assumptions; none match B550.
DeepSeek V4.1 Engram placement maps; they are incompatible with the 1017 checkpoint and unrelated to Qwen.

artifact_gate: Finish and size-verify the source checkpoint.

Produce or select a supported runnable Qwen GGUF artifact. The existing external GSQ-RCO artifact can be a performance control, but any RESMP-improved runnable artifact must come from the own-quantization pipeline before a product claim.
Stage the runnable GGUF/pack on ext4 NVMe scratch, not /mnt/weights; prior measurement showed HDD expert-slot random reads are 10.8x slower at queue depth 1.
Run the engine already built at /home/kearm/strata-main/build/qwen-sm86 or rebuild from the exact published Strata head after any change.
controls: Same model hashes, engine binary, prompt IDs, tokenizer, context, KV mode, speculative depth, expert profile, and storage path in every arm.
Restart the server between configurations and collect startup-selected layer split, cache slots, PCIe fractions, pool workers, and telemetry.
Use paired/interleaved runs with one discarded warm-up; report medians and dispersion, not a best run.
Keep both embedding replicas resident for the primary comparison. A later dedicated ceiling run may revisit that only by explicit service-owner decision.
benchmark_protocol.stage_a: Correctness and capacity: launch one GPU, verify representative output/function checks, record expert slots, VRAM, pinned arena, and PCIe probe.
benchmark_protocol.stage_b: Single-GPU controls: GPU0 and GPU1 separately; run tools/calibrate.py for pcie_frac, spec_min_p, workers, and adaptive tier. Use fresh and cached prompt paths.
benchmark_protocol.stage_c: Two-GPU mode selection: layer-split auto in both card orders, then manual split points around the auto choice (for a 48-layer model, typically 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 28, 30); separately test helper-expert mode.
benchmark_protocol.stage_d: Optimization stack: on the best two placements, compare --adapt-async 1, --pipeline-windows 2, STRATA_PF_FUSED=1, and STRATA_PREFILL_HELP=1 in separate arms before combining only winners.
benchmark_protocol.stage_e: Concurrency: --batch 2/4/8 with --batch-groups auto and explicit 1/2, measuring aggregate and per-request throughput.
workloads: cold fresh prefill: about 1.5K, 2K, 3K, 4K, 16K, 32K, and 128K tokens with nonce/no reuse
follow-up cached prefill and conversation restore
decode: temperature 0, 256-, 500-, and 1500-token outputs, at least five measured runs per arm after warm-up
multi-client aggregate decode with 2, 4, and 8 concurrent requests
metrics: prompt tok/s and TTFT from the server
decode tok/s, draft acceptance, and verified/generated counts
per-GPU utilization, memory, power, temperature, PCIe RX/TX
expert cache hit/miss, PCIe-share count, CPU pool rows, and helper-computed experts
stage handoff and adaptive-exchange timings where the engine exposes them

one_versus_two: Two cards should clearly help prefill by overlapping chunks and adding PCIe bandwidth, but single-stream decode should not be assumed 2x. It may be approximately equal if one card already holds the hot experts or if per-layer handoff dominates.
Two cards become more likely to win decode when the quantized expert set does not fit one cache; the second cache reduces CPU misses.
Aggregate multi-client throughput has the best chance of approaching the additional compute because batch groups can occupy both stages.

closest_published_strata_result.rig: 2x RTX 3090, no NVLink, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S, resident experts, int8 KV, spec 4 MTP
closest_published_strata_result.source: docs/MULTI_GPU.md, community report #1447; not reproduced on B550
closest_published_strata_result.interpretation: This is a target hypothesis of roughly 135-145 decode tok/s and 1.8K-2.3K prefill tok/s on a close but unequal 2x3090 rig, not a B550 claim. B550 has different CPU/RAM, asymmetric PCIe generations, and resident embedding services.
